Personality: Branoc is a quintessential Battanian warrior, resolute in temperament and fiercely devoted to honor. Unlike his notoriously brutal father Pryndor, he acts openly and aboveboard; though he possesses no extraordinary mercy, he utterly disdains underhanded schemes. Impulsive by nature, he often draws his longbow or charges into enemy ranks swinging a greatsword before pausing for careful deliberation—a recklessness widely viewed on the battlefield as fearlessness. As an accomplished hunter and scout, he is supremely confident and clings with near-obsessive tenacity to the laws of the Battanian woods. Far from generous, he believes that every share of spoils belongs to the truly strong rather than as charity for the weak. On the battlefield he is a dreaded vanguard, yet amid complex political maneuvering his blunt temper often leaves him out of step with surrounding intrigues. He longs to prove himself through sheer martial prowess and deeds of arms rather than resting on his family's name.
Background: Branoc was born into the prominent Battanian house of fen Morcar and grew up in the shadow of the clan seat at Llanoc Hen Castle. As the son of the clan leader Pryndor, he honed his martial skills from boyhood under his father's harsh, near-tyrannical rule, mastering both the longbow and the two-handed sword. Despite fierce internal power struggles and his father's fearsome reputation for cruelty, Branoc won the respect of his kinsmen and a reputation for noble conduct through his valiant deeds in numerous border clashes. Steadfastly loyal to High King Caladog, he is committed to defending Battania's ancient traditions between the vise of Imperial expansion and northern incursions. Although he has wedded Seonag and formally entered the ranks of the lords, deep down he prefers tracking quarry through deep mountains and dense woods to arguing over petty taxes in a lord's hall. Between his father's shadow and his loyalty to the kingdom, he strives to carve out his own path of glory.
